scope: Proposition 5.3 (Residue obstruction) of the manuscript “Global Spherical Shells on Minimal Surfaces of Class VII” (preprints/Global-Spherical-Shells-on-Minimal-Surfaces-of-Class-VII-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 060 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d441e45f773bce9f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 24-25. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix F ∈ {O, E} and rates (−ε, b) as in Theorem 5.2. For distinct closed irreducible curves Bi ⊂ Y bounded above in height, let ηi be nonzero holomorphic 24 differentials on their normalizations with coefficients in f∗ i F. Suppose their pushforward currents have negative-end mass exponents strictly smaller than b. Then the classes [Cηi ] ∈ H2,1 −ε,b(Y, F) are linearly independent: every finite subfamily is independent. For F = O, even one such differential is impossible.
